question: According to the available information, the Commission representation in Berlin alone has a six-strong press and public relations team; on top of this, there is another position at each of the regional representations in Bonn and Munich and two positions at the representation in Vienna.

These decentralised media operations exist in parallel with a generously staffed Spokesperson’s Service and DG COMM, which reports directly to the President; they communicate the Commission President’s messages straight to the accredited media in Brussels. 1.

How many press and media positions have been allocated to the representation in Berlin, the regional representations in Bonn and Munich and the representation in Vienna – broken down by full-time/part-time status and by employment category (officials, other staff, contract personnel)?

What tangible, measurable added value do these decentralised press operations bring with respect to the central communication apparatus made up of the Spokesperson’s Service and DG COMM, and based on what criteria – e.g. reach, media output, independent content – is this added value determined?

How does the Commission square this duplication of centralised and decentralised communication structures with the budgetary principles of economy and efficiency (Article 33 of the Financial Regulation)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.8.2026) The Commission’s Representations in the Member States operate under the guidance of the Directorate-General for Communication. They ensure communication activities at national level and engage with citizens, media and stakeholders on EU policies, in the national context.

The press team of the Commission’s Representation and regional offices in Germany comprises one official, one temporary agent, five contract agents and one local agent. Of these, three posts are full-time and five are part-time. The team in the Representation in Austria comprises one official and two contract agents, all full time.

The Commission’s Spokespersons’ Service (SPP) and the Representations’ press teams have distinct and complementary roles, in line with the Commission’s Working Methods1. The SPP is the contact point for the Brussels-based press corps.

The Representations’ press teams support the media in the Member States, providing tailored information that facilitates coverage by locally based journalists on EU policies with relevance for citizens and communities.

Daily close coordination between SPP and Representations ensures that media professionals in the Member States receive relevant information adapted to the national context, enabling them to better inform citizens about the EU.

The division of tasks enables the Commission to reach its communication objectives better and in a cost-effective way, in line with the Working Methods and the budgetary principles of the Financial Regulation2.
